title: Recalculating a Damage Repair Charge on a Security Deposit Account Statement
content:
When the damage repair charge on a Security Deposit Account final account statement is corrected, the repair credit is the repair charged less the corrected repair charge.

**Calculation.**

- **Repair charged.** The amount of the damage repair line itemized on the account.
- **Corrected repair charge.** The labor hours recorded on the repair line times the labor rate, plus the parts cost recorded on the line, rounded half up to the cent.
- **Labor rate.** The program's maintenance labor rate for damage repair, per hour.
- **Repair credit.** The repair charged less the corrected repair charge, rounded half up to the cent.

**Records read.** The damage repair line's amount, its recorded labor hours and its recorded parts cost (the line's replacement cost), from the account's itemized move-out lines. The deposit program of the account.

## Worked example (hypothetical line, labor rate taken as 65.00 USD per hour)

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Repair charged | 360.00 USD |
| Labor: 3.5 recorded hours times 65.00 | 227.50 |
| Parts cost recorded on the line | 80.00 |
| Corrected repair charge: 227.50 plus 80.00 | 307.50 |
| Repair credit: 360.00 less 307.50 | 52.50 USD |

## Second example (hypothetical, labor only)

A repair line of 150.00 USD carries 1.75 recorded hours and no parts. At 65.00 USD per hour the corrected repair charge is 113.75 USD, so the repair credit is 36.25 USD.
